    Advanced. This question goes beyond core Algebra I. It is not required by the course.

    Simplify i42i^{42}i42.

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: Multiplies the exponent by iii instead of reducing it.

    You chose B: Reduces correctly to i2i^2i2 but takes i2=1i^2 = 1i2=1 rather than −1-1−1.

    You chose D: Counts remainder 222 as the third cycle entry, landing on i3=−ii^3 = -ii3=−i.

    A power of iii depends only on the remainder of its exponent after division by 444. Since 42=4×10+242 = 4 \times 10 + 242=4×10+2, the remainder is 222, which lands on i2i^2i2.

    i42=i4×10+2=(i4)10⋅i2=110⋅i2=−1i^{42} = i^{4 \times 10 + 2} = \left(i^4\right)^{10} \cdot i^2 = 1^{10} \cdot i^2 = -1i42=i4×10+2=(i4)10⋅i2=110⋅i2=−1

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: Applies the minus to the real part only, giving −4+3=−1-4 + 3 = -1−4+3=−1.

    You chose C: Merges each number's real and imaginary parts into one before subtracting.

    You chose D: Subtracts in reverse order, giving the opposite of each part.

    Subtraction distributes the minus sign to both parts of the second number, so the imaginary parts give −4−3=−7-4 - 3 = -7−4−3=−7.

    (9−4i)−(5+3i)=(9−5)+(−4−3)i=4−7i(9 - 4i) - (5 + 3i) = (9 - 5) + (-4 - 3)i = 4 - 7i(9−4i)−(5+3i)=(9−5)+(−4−3)i=4−7i

    Correct answer: A

    So a=2a = 2a=2, b=−4b = -4b=−4, and c=−3c = -3c=−3.

  1. 1

    1. Two parts that keep their distance, and one operation that makes them meet . 9 points. This question goes beyond core Algebra I. It is not required by the course. Question 1 of 10.

    9 pts Advanced. This question goes beyond core Algebra I. It is not required by the course.

    Let z=5−3iz = 5 - 3iz=5−3i and w=−2+7iw = -2 + 7iw=−2+7i. Every answer below should end in standard form a+bia + bia+bi, with the real part first and a single imaginary term second.

    1. A
      Part A.

      Compute z+wz + wz+w and z−wz - wz−w.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    2. B
      Part B.

      Compute zwzwzw.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 3 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      A classmate looks at your sum from part A and says it can be simplified further, on the grounds that both of its terms are just numbers. Explain why the two parts of a complex number cannot be merged into one. Then explain why, despite that, the imaginary parts of zzz and www were able to change the REAL part of your answer in part B.

      Carry your own answer forward Argue from whichever results you reached in parts A and B, even if they were not the expected ones. The credit here is for the account of why the parts behave differently under the two operations, not for reproducing one particular pair of numbers.

      Explain why it works A sentence or two. Reasons, not steps. 3 points

    The answer

    Part A

    The answer

    Part A

    With bbb the base in feet, the height is 2b−32b - 32b−3 feet and the area sentence is 12b(2b−3)=27\tfrac{1}{2}b(2b - 3) = 2721​b(2b−3)=27, which in standard form is 2b2−3b−54=02b^2 - 3b - 54 = 02b2−3b−54=0.

    Part B

    The roots are b=6b = 6b=6 and b=−92b = -\dfrac{9}{2}b=−29​. Only b=6b = 6b=6 is a length, so the sail has a base of 666 feet and a height of 999 feet.

    Part C

    The rejected root satisfies the equation exactly; it fails only the meaning attached to the letter, since the model was built assuming bbb is a length and lengths are not negative. And no: the reject step is a test each root must be put to, not a quota. Some situations admit both roots.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Let bbb be the base in feet; the height is 2b−32b - 32b−3. Half the base times the height is 272727, so clear the fraction and gather to standard form.

    12b(2b−3)=27⟹2b2−3b−54=0.\frac{1}{2}b(2b - 3) = 27 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2b^2 - 3b - 54 = 0.21​b(2b−3)=27⟹2b2−3b−54=0.

    Part B

    Read the coefficients 222, −3-3−3, −54-54−54; the negative constant makes the −4ac-4ac−4ac term add.

    b=3±9+4324=3±214=6 or −92.b = \frac{3 \pm \sqrt{9 + 432}}{4} = \frac{3 \pm 21}{4} = 6 \text{ or } -\frac{9}{2}.b=43±9+432​​=43±21​=6 or −29​.

    A base cannot be negative, so keep b=6b = 6b=6. The height is 2(6)−3=92(6) - 3 = 92(6)−3=9, so the sail is 666 feet by 999 feet.

    Part C

    Substitute b=−92b = -\frac{9}{2}b=−29​ and the equation vanishes, so it is a genuine root:

    2(−92)2−3(−92)−54=54−54=0.2\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right)^2 - 3\left(-\frac{9}{2}\right) - 54 = 54 - 54 = 0.2(−29​)2−3(−29​)−54=54−54=0.

    What it fails is the meaning of the letter: naming bbb a base in feet restricted the answers to positive numbers, and the algebra never knew that. So no general rule follows. Rejecting a root is a test applied to each root, not a quota, and some situations, like a thrown object passing a height twice, admit both.

    In one line

    With bbb the base in feet, the model is 2b2−3b−54=02b^2 - 3b - 54 = 02b2−3b−54=0, whose roots are b=6b = 6b=6 and b=−92b = -\frac{9}{2}b=−29​. The sail has a base of 666 feet and a height of 999 feet, the second root being rejected because a base is a length and a length cannot be negative. That rejection is a test applied to each root, not a quota: a situation is free to admit both.

      Carry your own answer forward Solve whichever equation you produced in part A, and build the dimensions from your own expression for the second side. The credit here is for the rewrite, for keeping both signs at the root, and for turning each root back into a pair of dimensions.

      Solve and show your work Write each step out, and end with the value and its units. 4 points

    3. C
      Part C.

      Decide which of your two roots the situation admits, and defend the decision by testing each one against everything the yard requires. Then show how your standard form from part A could have told you, before you solved anything, what the signs of its two roots had to be, and contrast this problem with an ordinary area problem in that respect.

      Carry your own answer forward Test whichever roots you found against the yard, and read your own standard form from part A rather than the expected one. The credit here is for putting each root to the situation honestly, for the argument you draw from the coefficients, and for the contrast, not for a particular pair of numbers.

      Justify your claim State the claim, then give the reason it has to be true. 6 points

    The answer

    Part A

    With xxx the length in metres of each end, the side parallel to the wall is 44−2x44 - 2x44−2x metres, and x(44−2x)=240x(44 - 2x) = 240x(44−2x)=240 becomes x2−22x+120=0x^2 - 22x + 120 = 0x2−22x+120=0.

    Part B

    (x−11)2=1(x - 11)^2 = 1(x−11)2=1, so x=10x = 10x=10 and x=12x = 12x=12. The first gives a yard 101010 by 242424 metres and the second gives a yard 121212 by 202020 metres.

    • x=11±1x = 11 \pm 1x=11±1 is the same pair; a 101010 by 242424 yard and a 121212 by 202020 yard are the two shapes, and reporting only the value of xxx leaves the dimensions unstated

    Part C

    Both, since each gives positive dimensions and meets both requirements: two different yards fit the specification. The positive constant term makes the roots multiply to +120+120+120, so they share a sign, and their sum of +22+22+22 makes that sign positive. A negative constant term is what splits the signs and forces a root out.

    Worked solution

    Part A

    Let xxx be each end, in metres. The wall takes no fencing, so the parallel side is 44−2x44 - 2x44−2x, and the area is the two dimensions multiplied.

    x(44−2x)=240⟹x2−22x+120=0.x(44 - 2x) = 240 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^2 - 22x + 120 = 0.x(44−2x)=240⟹x2−22x+120=0.

    Dividing through by the leading −2-2−2 makes the x2x^2x2 stand alone for the square.

    Part B

    Complete the square: half of −22-22−22 is −11-11−11, (−11)2=121(-11)^2 = 121(−11)2=121, and −120+121=1-120 + 121 = 1−120+121=1.

    (x−11)2=1⟹x−11=±1⟹x=12 or 10.(x - 11)^2 = 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x - 11 = \pm 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad x = 12 \text{ or } 10.(x−11)2=1⟹x−11=±1⟹x=12 or 10.

    With the parallel side 44−2x44 - 2x44−2x: at x=10x = 10x=10 the yard is 101010 by 242424, and at x=12x = 12x=12 it is 121212 by 202020.

    Part C

    Both roots are admitted. At x=10x = 10x=10 the sides are 10,10,2410, 10, 2410,10,24; at x=12x = 12x=12 they are 12,12,2012, 12, 2012,12,20. Every length is positive, both use 444444 metres and enclose 240240240 square metres, so two different yards fit.

    The standard form knew this in advance. First check there are signs to read: the discriminant 484−480=4>0484 - 480 = 4 > 0484−480=4>0, so the roots are real. Then the sum and product, read off the coefficients,

    r1r2=120,r1+r2=22,r_1 r_2 = 120, \qquad r_1 + r_2 = 22,r1​r2​=120,r1​+r2​=22,

    show a positive product, so the roots share a sign, and a positive sum makes that sign positive. Both are positive, knowable from the coefficients alone. An ordinary area problem instead has a negative constant term, w2+kw−A=0w^2 + kw - A = 0w2+kw−A=0, whose roots multiply to a negative number and so have opposite signs, forcing one out.

    In one line

    With xxx the length of each end, the model is x2−22x+120=0x^2 - 22x + 120 = 0x2−22x+120=0, which rewrites as (x−11)2=1(x - 11)^2 = 1(x−11)2=1 and gives x=10x = 10x=10 and x=12x = 12x=12. Both are admitted: a 101010 by 242424 yard and a 121212 by 202020 yard each use 444444 metres of fencing and enclose 240240240 square metres. The positive constant term forces the roots to multiply to +120+120+120 and so to share a sign, which is exactly why nothing had to be discarded here, unlike an area problem whose negative constant term splits the roots and rules one out.
